the $4000 display buffer: the bitmap, the screen matrix at $6000 and the colours at $6400, filled by unpack_picture and the text
MAIN's bytes past WON, left from the game (MAIN $6400-$A4FF; WON loads over $6800-$7DFF and the pictures over $8400-$ACFF); the ending never reads them
left from the game: SEG0 or SEG1 past F3.PAC (the overlay at $A500-$BCFF), SPB at $BD00-$BEFF and the disk text buffer at $BF00; the ending never reads them
the $C000 display buffer: the bitmap (under the I/O from $D000), the screen matrix at $E000 and the colours at $E400
left from flight: the model heap and INIT ($E900-$EAFF), which the ending never reads
EXTERN's bytes between the two halves of the line table, which build_line_table writes over EXTERN at $EB00-$EBC7 and $EC00-$ECC7
the rest of EXTERN past the line table, left from the game
left from the game: the text cache from side 2 ($F600-$F9FF) and the per-frame work buffers ($FA00 on); the ending never reads them

The high seven bits of the dissolves' 15-bit shift register, Y holding the low eight: bits 0-4 pick a page of the 8 KB bitmap, bits 5-6 the pixel pair in the byte. It starts at $7FFF, shifts right with taps $60 into this byte, and stops when it comes back, so every nonzero value comes once

The playing note's frequency, high byte

Not data: BIT $1EA5 at $7022 hides LDA $1E (show_drawn, $7023) in its operand
Not data: BIT $40A9 at $701F and at $7072 hides LDA #$40, the entries show_4000 ($7020) and clear_4000 ($7073)
The $4000 buffer's screen matrix ($6000-$63E7); clear_drawing's patched STA at $7080 was left pointing here after clearing the bitmap below

WON's first instruction: SR loads WON over MAIN and jumps here ($154B) when the ship docks in the Manchi system. Sets up the interrupt and the line table, loads FONT and the three pictures F1-F3, clears the $4000 bitmap, turns the multicolour bitmap on, shows the empty $4000 buffer, makes the colour RAM white and goes on to the first page ($7462)
load_inline's argument: load to $F200, then the file name "FONT" and a zero
Loads "F1.PAC" to $8400
load_inline's argument: load to $8400, then the file name "F1.PAC" and a zero
Loads "F2.PAC" to $9200
load_inline's argument: load to $9200, then the file name "F2.PAC" and a zero
Loads "F3.PAC" to $A100
load_inline's argument: load to $A100, then the file name "F3.PAC" and a zero
With the files in: clears the $4000 bitmap, sets the bitmap mode, shows the empty $4000 buffer with its colours, whitens the colour RAM and jumps to the first page
Banks the I/O and the KERNAL in ($01 low bits %110, RAM at $A000), keeping A
Banks all RAM in ($01 low bits %100), keeping A

Loads the file named after the JSR: two bytes of load address (low, high), then the name ending in a zero, and returns past the zero. LOAD runs from device 8 with secondary address 0, so the file goes to that address whatever its header says, and is retried until the KERNAL reports no error; the caller's $30/$31 are kept in the patched loads at $68C4 and $68C8
The name's length, patched in by $688F
The name's address, low byte, patched in by $6897
The name's address, high byte, patched in by $689E
The load address's low byte, patched in by $6873
The load address's high byte, patched in by $6879
The caller's $30, patched in by $685B and put back on the way out
The caller's $31, patched in by $6860
Clears any key waiting, waits for the interrupt to put one in key ($3C), clears it again and returns it in A
Sets key ($3C) to $FF: none waiting

A wait of about 0.86 seconds that a key ends early (the key stays in $3C). clear_key leaves A at $FF, so the caller's A makes no difference: the 26-cycle loop always runs 255 + 254 + ... + 1 = 32,640 times (848,640 cycles), and the interrupt adds its share
Prints the character in A at the cursor, keeping A, the flags, and X and Y (put back by the patched loads at $6908 and $690A)
The caller's X, patched in by $6902
The caller's Y, patched in by $68FF

Draws character A (bit 7 ignored) into the drawing buffer at the cursor: RETURN ($0D) starts a new line, $08 and $7F rub out the character before the cursor, and a character that would pass the window's right edge starts a new line first. Its 8 bytes are copied from FONT ($F200 + 8 × the character) into the bitmap cell, and the cursor moves on a column
The cursor row's offset in a bitmap, low byte, patched in from char_row_offsets ($6957); the ADC adds the column's offset to it
The cursor row's offset, high byte, ORed with the drawing buffer's page ($695F)
The character's address in FONT, low byte, patched in by $6945
The character's address in FONT, high byte: built from character × 8 and then $F2 added ($694D)
The bitmap cell's address, low byte, patched in by $696C
The bitmap cell's address, high byte, patched in by $6973

Rubs out the character before the cursor: prints a space at the cursor, steps back two columns, prints another and steps back one, leaving the cursor a column to the left (the BPL at $6990 lands on the next instruction either way)

Moves the cursor to the window's left column on the next row. Past row 24 it scrolls the drawing buffer's rows 1-24 up a character row instead (7,680 bytes) and clears only the first 64 bytes of the bottom row, 8 of its 40 cells: $69F0 loads Y = 1 where the 320-byte row needs 2
new_line's scroll source, low byte, set to $40 (row 1 starts 320 bytes in)
new_line's scroll source page, the drawing buffer's plus one, stepped on each page
new_line's scroll destination page, the drawing buffer's own, stepped on each page
The bottom row's address, low byte, set to zero
The bottom row's page, the drawing buffer's plus $1E (row 24 starts 7,680 bytes in)
The byte counter new_line's two loops count down

With interrupts off, points every vector at the ending's own handlers: a raster interrupt at line $50 with CIA1's interrupts off; the NMI and BRK vectors at the RTI at $6A65 (it also writes that address to $FFFC, which a reset never reads from RAM); the KERNAL's IRQ vector ($0314) at irq_body and the hardware one ($FFFE) at irq. Then clears the key, sets up the SID (sound_init) and banks all RAM in. The first call of the ending ($6800)
An RTI: the NMI (RESTORE) and BRK do nothing
The raster interrupt as the hardware vector enters it, with all RAM banked in: pushes A, X and Y as the KERNAL's entry would and goes on into irq_body

The raster interrupt as $0314 enters it, the KERNAL having pushed the registers: saves $01, banks the I/O in, acknowledges the raster, scans the keyboard (a new or repeating key goes to key without bit 7), counts the frame in $3D, runs the effect player and returns

Scans the keyboard matrix itself; returns C set with a key's code in A when a key is new or repeating, C clear otherwise. CTRL and the two SHIFTs are read first and masked out of their rows; the first key held, row 7 down to row 0 and bit 7 down to bit 0 within a row, is numbered 8 × the row's place + the bit's and looked up in key_codes, or key_codes_shifted with either SHIFT, CTRL keeping only the low five bits. A held key repeats 36 frames after it went down, then every 6. Port A is left an input
BIT $E8 hides an INX ($E8) at $6AEA: the first pass skips it and the BCS at $6AEC lands on it, so X counts the row's released keys from bit 7 down to the one held
The last key's number, $FF for none
Frames left before a held key first repeats: 30 from a new key
Frames left before the next repeat: 6
For each row in scan order (7 down to 0), the bits of its modifier keys, ORed in so they never count as a key: CTRL in row 7, right SHIFT in row 6, left SHIFT in row 1
CTRL's bit from row 7, zero while it is held
Right SHIFT's bit from row 6, zero while it is held
Left SHIFT's bit from row 1, zero while it is held

The 64 keys' codes in scan order (row 7 bit 7 first): ASCII for letters (lower case), digits and punctuation, $0D for RETURN, $7F for DEL, $08 for the left-arrow key, $1B for F1, $09 and $0A for the cursor keys, and $80 for the keys with no code, which arrive as 0 since the interrupt keeps seven bits. The ending only waits for any key
The same with a SHIFT held: capitals, the symbols over the digits, $0B for cursor up and $08 for cursor left

Wipes the window's character rows X to Y off to the left: the rows slide a cell at a time (wipe_left_step), the two buffers taking turns so that each flip shows one more cell, until the window's width has gone. The ending uses it once, on the Emperor's speech ($7B64)
Moves character rows $36 to $38 - 1 of the drawing buffer one cell left within the window, clearing its right-hand cell
Wipes the window's character rows X to Y off to the right, as wipe_left does to the left: after the landing ($7584) and after the Golden Sunburst page ($7C1C)
Moves character rows $36 to $38 - 1 one cell right within the window, clearing its left-hand cell

Scrolls the window's character rows X to Y up and away, two pixel lines a step, showing each step with its colours (show_drawn_colours) and catching the other buffer up; the ending uses it once, after Hiathra's arrival ($7A66)
Moves the window's pixel lines up two through the line table, then clears the bottom two (clear_line)
Clears pixel line X of the window in the drawing buffer
Scrolls the window's character rows X to Y down and away, two pixel lines a step, as scroll_up does upwards: three times in the ending ($7804, $7904, $7D0C)
Moves the window's pixel lines down two, working from the bottom up, then clears the top two
Copies the colours to the colour RAM, then runs copy_matrix; nothing calls it

Copies 8 pages, a buffer's $2000-$27FF (screen matrix and colours), from page A ORed with $12 to the same place in the other buffer. Only dissolve_in calls it, with A = $1E, which makes the source $E000 whichever buffer is shown
copy_matrix's source page, patched in and stepped
copy_matrix's destination page, the source's with bit 7 flipped
Copies the $4000 buffer's picture to the $C000 buffer and the colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Copies the $C000 buffer's picture to the $4000 buffer and the colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Copies the shown buffer's picture to the drawing buffer (copy_shown) and its colours to the colour RAM, so the next page of text is drawn over the same picture
Copies the $4000 buffer's picture, bitmap, screen matrix and colours ($28 pages), to the $C000 buffer
Copies the $C000 buffer's picture to the $4000 buffer
Copies the shown buffer's picture to the drawing buffer
The picture copy's source page, patched in and stepped

The picture copy's destination page, patched in and stepped
Sets $34/$35 to column A × 8

row_address's caller's X, patched in by $6E52
Fills the colour RAM, $D800-$DBFF, with 1 (white), interrupts off
The page of white_colours' STA, stepped from $D8; the snapshot shows it left at $DC
Copies a block, $14 bytes wide and $15 rows high, from ($10) into the colour RAM at column X of row Y (colour_rows), the source advancing by the width each row; nothing in the ending calls it
put_colour_block's destination, low byte, patched in and stepped by 40
put_colour_block's destination, high byte

Copies a block, $14 bytes wide and $15 rows high, from ($10) into the drawing buffer's screen matrix at column X of row Y (matrix_rows), the source advancing by block_stride ($66) each row; entered at $6ECD for the $C000 buffer and $6ED1 for the $4000 one. Nothing in the ending calls it
put_matrix_block's destination, low byte, patched in and stepped by 40
put_matrix_block's destination, high byte
Builds the pixel-line table at $EB00 (low bytes) and $EC00 (high): for each of the 200 lines, (line / 8) × 320 + line mod 8
The offset build_line_table is working on, low byte; it leaves $1F40 (8,000) in the pair
The offset build_line_table is working on, high byte
Each character row's offset in a bitmap, 320 × the row, a word each for rows 0-24 (print_char, row_address)
char_row_offsets read from one byte on, for the high bytes (X = 2 × the row)
Each row's address in the colour RAM, $D800 + 40 × the row, a word each (put_colour_block)
colour_rows read from one byte on, for the high bytes
Each row's offset from a buffer's page to its screen matrix, $2000 + 40 × the row, a word each (put_matrix_block)
matrix_rows read from one byte on, for the high bytes

Turns the multicolour bitmap on ($D011 bit 5, $D016 bit 4), with the bitmap at the start of the VIC's bank and the screen matrix $2000 into it ($D018 = $80), and the background black. Its read-modify-write of $D011 also writes back bit 7, which reads as bit 8 of the beam's line and writes bit 8 of the raster compare: run while the beam is on line 256 or later, it moves the interrupt from line $50 to $150 (336), which no frame reaches, and the interrupt stops for good
Shows the $C000 buffer and copies its colours to the colour RAM; nothing calls it
Shows the $4000 buffer and copies its colours to the colour RAM
Shows the drawing buffer (show_drawn) and copies its colours to the colour RAM: the step after each page of the ending is drawn

Shows the $C000 buffer (the VIC's bank 3, CIA2 port A bits 0-1 = 0) and makes $4000 the drawing buffer. The BITs that follow hide two more entries in their operands, show_4000 (LDA #$40) and show_drawn (LDA $1E). Sets $3A to the shown buffer's page, $12 to its screen matrix's and $1E to the other buffer's
BIT $40A9: its operand is LDA #$40, show_4000's entry
Shows the $4000 buffer (the VIC's bank 1, CIA2 port A bits 0-1 = %10) and makes $C000 the drawing buffer; the LDA #$40 here is the operand of the BIT at $701F
BIT $1EA5: its operand is LDA $1E, show_drawn's entry
Shows the drawing buffer, the shown one becoming the drawing buffer: the flip after each page is drawn; the LDA $1E here is the operand of the BIT at $7022
Clears the drawing buffer's bitmap, 32 pages; the BITs that follow hide entries for the $4000 buffer ($7073) and the $C000 one ($7076). Only clear_4000 is called
BIT $40A9: its operand is LDA #$40, clear_4000's entry
Clears the $4000 buffer's bitmap ($4000-$5FFF), called once at the start ($6834); the LDA #$40 here is the operand of the BIT at $7072
BIT $C0A9: its operand is LDA #$C0, an entry at $7076 for the $C000 buffer
The page clear_drawing's STA writes, patched in and stepped; the snapshot shows it left at $60

Brings the drawing buffer's picture onto the shown one a pixel pair at a time in a scattered order: after copy_matrix, a 15-bit shift register visits every pixel pair of the 8 KB bitmap once (dissolve_lfsr). Called once, as the Manchi bow to the egg ($7708)
The pixel pair from the drawing buffer, patched into this ORA by $70CA
The four pixel pairs of a multicolour byte, left to right
The bits each pixel pair leaves alone, the complements of pixel_masks
Fades the shown picture to black a pixel pair at a time, in the shift register's scattered order: before the bowing Manchi dissolve in ($7705) and before the palace is shown ($7A56)
The complements of pixel_masks again, for dissolve_out

Unpacks the picture packed at page A into the drawing buffer: a byte below $80 is a count and the next byte is repeated that many times; $80 plus a count is followed by that many bytes to copy; a zero is followed by the border colour, which is stored too, written to $D020, and ends it. A whole picture is a buffer's bitmap, its screen matrix at +$2000 and its colours at +$2400

Copies the shown buffer's colours (its +$2400) to the colour RAM: first to $0C00 with all RAM banked in, then on to $D800 with the I/O in, since the RAM under the KERNAL and the colour RAM cannot both be seen at once
colours_to_ram's source page, the shown buffer's plus $24, stepped
colours_to_ram's staging page, from $0C, stepped
The staging page read back, from $0C, stepped
The colour RAM page written, from $D8, stepped
Silences the SID's three voices, turns the filter off and the volume up (15), and sets up the effect player and the masks
Starts sound effect A (0-4; others are ignored) on voice 1, copying its settings from the effect tables to $80-$8C with interrupts off

The effect player, run by the interrupt every frame: starts each repeat of the effect's note (frequency, envelope, waveform, gate), moves the frequency by the step each frame, releases the gate at the release point and silences the note when its frames run out. Below that, a second sound left in from a shared driver slides $74/$75 up 2 a frame towards $72/$73 and would play it while no effect is, but drone_mask is zero, so it never sounds. The ending starts no effect, so the player has nothing to play
Each effect's starting frequency, low byte, for effects 0-4
Effect 4's starting frequency, low byte, set by tone ($7433)
Each effect's starting frequency, high byte: $10, $18, $01, $80, and effect 4's
Effect 4's starting frequency, high byte, set by tone ($7436)
Each effect's frequency step per frame, low byte
Each effect's step, high byte: effect 0 falls by $80 a frame, effect 1 rises by $80, effect 2 falls by 2, effect 3 rises by $600, effect 4 holds
Each effect's attack and decay
Each effect's sustain and release
Each effect's waveform with the gate: noise ($81) for effects 0, 2 and 3, pulse ($41) for 1 and 4

Effect 4's note length, set by tone and silence ($7430)
The frames-left count at which each effect releases its gate
How many notes each effect plays: three for effect 1, one for the rest
Plays effect 3, rising noise, and waits for it: the intro's airlock sound, which the ending carries in its copy of the library and never calls
Plays effect 1, three rising tones: the intro's alert, never called here
Plays effect 0, two 18-frame silences and effect 0 again: the intro's explosion, never called here
Plays effect 0, falling noise; only explosion_sound calls it
Plays effect 2, noise falling slowly for 128 frames: the intro's rumble, never called here
Plays effect A and waits until it has finished or a key is pressed; if a key is already waiting it plays nothing

Sends morse_text with tones (the elements' routines in morse_routines) until its closing zero or a key, which is then cleared: the intro's distress beacon. Nothing in the ending calls it, so its patched operands still hold the file's $FF00
The Morse character's address, low byte, patched in and stepped
The Morse character's address, high byte
The element routine's address, low byte, patched into this JSR from morse_routines
The element routine's address, high byte

The distress call, SOS SOS PLAY ULTIMA SOS SOS: $AE a dot and $AD a dash, $A7 a short gap between the letters of SOS, $A0 a gap between the other letters and $AF a gap between words (the five codes are morse_symbols)
The five Morse characters distress_call looks up, in morse_routines' order: dot, dash, gap, word gap, short gap
The Morse elements' routines, a word each: morse_dot, morse_dash, morse_gap, silence_18 and silence_4
morse_routines read from one byte on, for the high bytes (Y = 2 × the element)
A dot: a 2-frame tone and 2 frames of silence
A dash: a 6-frame tone and 2 frames of silence
The gap between letters: 6 frames of silence
18 frames of silence (effect 4 at frequency 0): the gap between Morse words and the pause in explosion_sound
4 frames of silence, the gap between the letters of SOS
A tone at frequency $3864 lasting A frames
A frames of silence: effect 4 at frequency 0
Prints the text after the JSR, through the patched load at $744E, up to its zero, and returns to the instruction after the zero; the same routine as the intro's, at another address
The inline text's address, low byte, taken from the return address and stepped
The inline text's address, high byte
The ending's first page: unpacks F1, the landing among the Manchi warriors, into the $C000 buffer and prints the landing text full width, columns 1-38, from row 16
Puts the cursor on row 3, column 1, and then, after setting the window, on row 16, column 1: the first setting is never used

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero, spaces padding each line to the window's 38 columns: "With the Manchi queen's egg safely stowed in anti-crash webbing, you soar through the low-oxygen atmosphere of the Manchi homeworld. On a plain of red dust and obsidian mesas, you step out, the first human to reach this distant planet."
text_landing's closing zero, where print_inline's patched load at $744E was left when the snapshot was taken
Shows the landing with its colours, copies it to the other buffer, waits for a key, wipes rows 16-22 off to the right and prints the patrol from row 17

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: "The Manchi warrior-caste patrol shows little regard for this high achievement. From bandoliers of webbing they pull chitinous projectile weapons. You fear your mission will end all too soon..."
Shows the patrol, unpacks F2, the Manchi raising the egg, into the drawing buffer and prints the egg text beside it in a narrow window, columns 24-38 from row 3

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero, nine lines of the 15-column window: "...Until you bring forth the egg. The Manchi instantly lower their weapons and bow down before their revered Chi-gonger."
Waits for a key, fades the landing to black (dissolve_out), dissolves F2's page in (dissolve_in), copies it to the other buffer and prints the cry from row 16, columns 1-38
Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: '"Where did you get THAT?" someone cries.'
After a pause (the $0F it passes makes it no shorter), shows the cry, copies it and prints the interpreter text after it

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: two RETURNs, then "Have the Manchi learned the human tongue? Then you notice a Baakili trader shoving his way through the growing throng. An interpreter!"
After a pause (it passes $14, which changes nothing), shows the interpreter, copies it, waits for a key, scrolls rows 16-22 down and away (scroll_down) and prints Koth's plot from row 16

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero, six full lines: "With the trader's help, you expose Koth's plot and state your intention to restore the egg to its rightful owners. The Manchi gratefully accept it and raise it high above their heads for all to see."

Shows the plot, copies it, waits for a key, scrolls rows 16-21 down and away and sets only the row, 16: text_plot's six full lines left the column past the window's edge, so the first character starts a new line and the truce begins on row 17
Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: "Satisfied that her egg is safe once more, the Manchi queen calls a truce." Two RETURNs, then "Peace is at hand."
Shows the truce, unpacks F3, Emperor Hiathra holding up the Golden Sunburst, into the drawing buffer and prints the journey from row 1, column 1

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: "After a journey of many months, you arrive at the palace on the Imperial homeworld, where a hero's welcome awaits you. Standing before his throne, Emperor Hiathra speaks..."

Waits for a key, fades the Manchi to black and shows F3's page at once with its colours, copies it, waits for a key, scrolls rows 1-5 up and away (scroll_up) and prints the Emperor's speech from row 1

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: '"Honored traveler, our mightiest fleets could not accomplish what you achieved alone. Your bravery and cleverness are renowned throughout the Empire. I bestow upon you our highest honor: the Golden Sunburst of Valor."'
Shows the speech, copies it, waits for a key, wipes rows 1-6 off to the left and prints the medal's history from row 1

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: "The Golden Sunburst! In all of history only one other living person has earned this medal -- Admiral Koth. Too bad the slime escaped the Imperial Guard!"
Shows the medal's history, copies it, waits for a key, wipes rows 1-5 off to the right and prints the presentation from row 1
Loads X = 1 and Y = 5 again, the wipe's rows, which nothing then uses

Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: 'Hiathra places the coveted amulet around your neck. "The gratitude of the Imperium is yours!" he says, gesturing toward the crowd behind you. "Turn now, and accept the accolades that are your due!"'
Shows the presentation, copies it, waits for a key, scrolls rows 1-6 down and away and prints the last page from row 2
Text for print_inline, high-bit ASCII ending in a zero: "Cheers swell to fill the palace courtyard..." Two RETURNs, then "VICTORY IS YOURS!", centred
Shows the last page and waits for a key; then loads TITLE to $2000 and jumps to it, so the game goes back to its title
load_inline's argument: load to $2000, then the file name "TITLE" and a zero
